school: J. F. Drake State Community and Technical College
document_title: J.F. Drake State Community and Technical College Financial Statements, September 30, 2024 (institution-held figure); foundation figure read from the prior-year opening balance in Drake State Community & Technical College Annual Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended September 30, 2025
page: FY2024 report: 13 (Statement of Net Position), 15 (Endowment Income), 4 and 6 (auditor's report). FY2025 report (https://www.accs.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/DRAKE-FY25.pdf): 68 (foundation endowment roll-forward), 28 (foundation statement of financial position), 5 and 7 (auditor's report dated January 15, 2026)
quote: FY2024 Statement of Net Position, Non-Current Assets: 'Endowment Investments 209,743'. FY2025 report, Note 11 (Drake State Technical College Foundation, Inc.): 'Endowment net assets at December 31, 2023 $38,334' ... 'Endowment net assets at December 31, 2024 $271,734'.
arithmetic: 209,743 (college-held endowment investments at 9/30/2024) + 38,334 (foundation endowment net assets at 12/31/2023, the foundation year end that falls inside the FY2024 window) = 248,077.
reporting_entity: The college for the $209,743. The $38,334 is for Drake State Technical College Foundation, Inc., which the FY2024 report does not include; it first appears as a discretely presented component unit in the FY2025 report.
caveats: Confidence is medium for three reasons. (1) The foundation figure is not from an FY2024 statement: it is the opening balance (12/31/2023) of the endowment roll-forward in the FY2025 report, which I am using only for its prior-year figure. The foundation has a December 31 year end, so the college figure (9/30/2024) and foundation figure (12/31/2023) are nine months apart; by 12/31/2024 the foundation endowment was $271,734 after $225,000 of contributions. (2) The foundation's own calendar-2023 Form 990 says its statements were not audited and answers 'No' to holding endowments, which conflicts with the $38,334 opening balance. (3) In the FY2024 college statements the $209,743 is captioned 'Endowment Investments' but the matching net position line 'Restricted - Nonexpendable Scholarships' is printed with a dash, and there is no endowment note. If only the FY2024 audited statement is to be relied on, the defensible figure is the institution-held $209,743.
form_990_crosscheck: Cross-check only, not audited: Drake State Technical College Foundation Inc (EIN 63-1002142) Form 990 for calendar 2023 (ProPublica object ID 202403139349304300): total and net assets $384,250 at 12/31/2023; Part IV line 10 (endowments) answered 'No'; Part XII line 2b (audited statements) answered 'No'. Calendar 2024 Form 990: net assets $1,520,937. These do not agree with the FY2025 audited report, which shows foundation net assets of $478,508 at the start of 2024 and $2,421,060 at 12/31/2024.

document_title: Alamo Community College District Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Years Ended August 31, 2024 and 2023
page: 44 (District Statements of Net Position); 45 (Exhibit 1A, Foundation Statements of Financial Position); 52 (Note 1, reporting entity); 91, 94, 96-98, 102 (Note 25, Foundation notes); 23-26 (auditor's report)
quote: District net position (8/31/2024) has 'Restricted for: Expendable' lines only, no nonexpendable or endowment line. Note 1: 'The Alamo Colleges Foundation, Inc. ... sole purpose is to provide benefits such as scholarships and grants to the students, faculty and staff of the District.' Note 25G: 'The Foundation's endowment consists of 222 individual funds'; 'As of December 31, 2023 Endowment funds: [without donor restrictions] $421,867; Non-endowed Funds $43,432,716; Accumulated Gains $10,127,562; Endowed Funds $24,966,744; Total $78,948,889'. Note 25C: 'Endowments invested in perpetuity (24,966,744)'.
arithmetic: No value computed. The audited report gives district-wide foundation figures only (endowed funds $24,966,744; with accumulated gains $10,127,562 that is $35,094,306; total foundation net assets $78,948,889, all as of 12/31/2023) and contains no schedule dividing any of them among the five colleges. No district figure has been allocated to St Philip's.
reporting_entity: Alamo Community College District (five colleges, one audited report) and its discretely presented component unit, Alamo Colleges Foundation, Inc. (December 31 year end). Not St Philip's College on its own.
caveats: No endowment is attributable to St Philip's specifically in any audited document I could find. The District itself holds no endowment (no nonexpendable net position). All endowment sits in the district-wide Alamo Colleges Foundation, whose figures in the District's FY2024 report are as of December 31, 2023. The foundation note's table is loosely labelled: it lists every class of foundation net assets under the row label 'Endowment funds', so the endowment could be read as $24,966,744 (corpus only), $35,094,306 (corpus plus accumulated gains) or, least plausibly, $78,948,889 (all net assets, including $43,432,716 of non-endowed restricted funds). The foundation's stand-alone audited statements are available only on request from the District's Finance and Fiscal Services department, so I could not read its own endowment note. Note 25N says Title III and Title V grant funds are kept in segregated accounts within the Foundation, which may include a St Philip's Title III endowment, but no amount is given. A fund list on the foundation site that might identify St Philip's funds returned a 404 error. St Philip's-only endowment would have to be requested from the Foundation or the District.

page: 80 (Schedule 4, Law Center column); 84 (Schedule 6, cash flows by campus); 62-64 (Notes 14-16); 5-8 (auditor's report)
quote: Schedule 4, 'LAW CENTER' column: 'Finance purchase obligations' blank; 'Lease liability' blank; 'Notes payable' blank; noncurrent liabilities are 'Compensated absences payable 2,652,903', 'Net pension liability 18,117,503', 'OPEB Liability 16,806,790', 'Total noncurrent liabilities 37,577,196'. 'Capital assets, net 7,363,928' equals 'Net investment in capital assets 7,363,928'.
arithmetic: bonds 0 + notes/loans 0 + finance leases/financed purchases 0 = 0. Check: the three non-debt lines sum to the column's total noncurrent liabilities (2,652,903 + 18,117,503 + 16,806,790 = 37,577,196), and net investment in capital assets equals capital assets, so no capital debt is netted.
reporting_entity: Southern University System (system-wide audit); the figure is the Law Center column of the audited report's combining schedule by campus.
caveats: Campus figures come from Schedule 4, 'Combining Schedule of Net Position, by Campus, June 30, 2024', which is supplementary information; the Legislative Auditor's opinion on it is that it is 'fairly stated, in all material respects, in relation to the basic financial statements as a whole' (PDF p.7-8), not a separate campus-level opinion. The System as a whole does carry direct-borrowing debt of $19,854,617 (notes payable $989,617 + finance purchase obligations $18,865,000, Note 14, PDF p.62), all shown in the Agricultural & Mechanical College (Baton Rouge) and Shreveport columns; the Shreveport column also carries the only lease liability ($1,272,460). Excluded, not debt: compensated absences, net pension liability, OPEB liability. The FY2024 audit was issued very late (auditor's report dated December 15, 2025, about 17.5 months after year end); beginning net position was restated (Note 18, PDF p.67) and the LLA summary says the statements are fairly stated 'as adjusted'. Bonds of the Southern University System Foundation (Millennium Housing, $18,865,000 principal plus premium) are the Foundation's, financed Baton Rouge and Shreveport facilities, and are mirrored on the System's books as finance purchase obligations in those two campus columns only. Schedule 6 shows no debt principal or interest paid in the Law Center column.

document_title: Bluefield State University Financial Statements and Required Supplementary Information, Years Ended June 30, 2024 and 2023
page: 15 (Statements of Net Position); 17 (cash flows); 39-41 (Notes 7 and 8); 49-50 (Note 10); 3-5 (auditor's report)
quote: Note 8 Long-Term Liabilities, 2024 ending balances: 'Accrued Compensated Absences 1,086,309; OPEB Liability (Asset) (263,017); Net Pension Liability 187,228; Subscription Liability 313,859; Total Noncurrent Liabilities 1,324,379'. Note 10: 'Although the bonds remain as a capital obligation of the Commission, an estimate of the obligation of each institution is reported as a long-term payable by each institution and as a receivable by the Commission. Amounts due to Commission at June 30, 2023 and 2022 is $-0-.'
arithmetic: bonds 0 + notes/loans 0 + finance leases 0 = 0. The statement of net position and Note 8 list no bonds, notes, loans or lease obligations; the only contractual liability is the subscription (SBITA) liability of $313,859, which is excluded by definition.
reporting_entity: The campus: Bluefield State University's own audited statements (including its blended Applied Research Foundation; the Bluefield State University Foundation is discretely presented).
caveats: System revenue bonds for West Virginia college facilities are obligations of the Higher Education Policy Commission / Municipal Bond Commission; the University was assessed $10,846 for that debt service in FY2024 but reports no payable for it. The $-0- sentence in Note 10 is printed with the dates 'June 30, 2023 and 2022' in the FY2024 report, which looks like text carried forward unchanged; the 2024 statement of net position confirms no long-term payable to the Commission (only a current 'Due to the Commission 27,913'). Excluded, not debt: subscription liability $313,859, compensated absences $1,086,309, net pension liability $187,228. Capital assets ($44,973,025) exceed net investment in capital assets ($43,034,458) by $1,938,567; only $313,859 of that is the subscription liability and the report does not itemise the rest (no borrowing is disclosed, so it is presumably capital-related payables). During FY2024 the Foundation transferred student housing assets of $5,003,823 to the University for no consideration; the Foundation had paid off the related Collegiate Housing note payable in FY2023, so no debt came with the assets.

school: University of the District of Columbia
document_title: University of the District of Columbia Basic Financial Statements for the Fiscal Years Ended September 30, 2024 and 2023 (With Independent Auditor's Report Therein), transmitted as DC Office of the Inspector General report OIG No. 24-1-23GG
page: 20 (Statements of Net Position); 11 and 19 (MD&A); 52-53 (lease and subscription notes); 8-10 (auditor's report); 3 (OIG transmittal)
quote: Statement of Net Position 2024: 'Lease liabilities - current portion 7,652,223'; 'Long-term lease liabilities 19,405,295'; 'Long-term subcription liabilities 557,302'; 'Other long-term liabilities 9,571'; 'Total Noncurrent Liabilities 19,972,168' (no bonds or notes payable lines). MD&A: 'The University does not have any debt related to its capital assets.' and 'the University has no separate long-term borrowing authority.'
arithmetic: bonds 0 + notes/loans 0 + finance leases/financed purchases 0 = 0. Lease liabilities of 7,652,223 + 19,405,295 = 27,057,518 are right-to-use (GASB 87) leases of buildings, equipment and a ground lease and are not counted, per the brief's exclusion of operating-type leases.
reporting_entity: The University's own audited statements (a component unit of the Government of the District of Columbia), with its two foundations discretely presented.
caveats: Confidence is medium because two definitional choices sit behind the zero, although the amounts themselves were read directly. (1) Leases: the University reports $27,057,518 of GASB 87 lease liabilities at 9/30/2024. GASB 87 does not separate finance from operating leases; I treated these as operating-type (rented space and a ground lease, no transfer of ownership, no financed purchases reported) and excluded them. If lease liabilities are to be counted as debt, the figure would be $27,057,518. (2) District financing: the University's capital programme is 'financed through funding sources provided by the District' ($35,667,956 of capital appropriations in FY2024; six-year plan of $317.0 million). Any bonds behind that funding are obligations of the District, and neither the University's statements nor the District's FY2024 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (I searched every mention of the University in it) allocates any District debt to the University. The two MD&A sentences quoted are in the unaudited MD&A; the absence of bonds and notes is on the audited statement of net position. The 2023 comparative column is labelled 'Restated'. Excluded, not debt: subscription liabilities $990,698, compensated absences $8,901,301.
